claims.objects: An abstract ordinary Hodge-atom ledger: a type of varieties with a dimension, a rationality predicate, the product with a projective line, and the multiplicity with which an atom occurs in the atomic composition of a variety; together with the residue discriminant and the parity ranks of an atom, and the explicit rational residue matrices of the cubic zero packet and of a curve of genus at least two.

claims.conclusion: Lean evaluates the residue discriminant of the cubic zero-packet residue as four ninths and of every curve residue as zero, derives from that separation and the parity ranks that the cubic atom occurs on no variety of dimension at most two, and concludes that the product of the cubic threefold with a projective line is not rational.

The surface and curve analysis of the manuscript, which uses the point-blowup and projective-bundle formulas, the nef-canonical lemma, and the classification of minimal smooth projective surfaces, enters as the two exclusion premises.

claims.conclusion: The supplied opaque geometric packet is packaged with a kernel-checked integral Smith witness for the five-axis Gram matrix, including explicit two-sided inverse row and column matrices and diagonal diag(1,6,6,6,6). Independently, for every F2-module T, Lean proves that the kernel of the tensor-extended five-axis Gram map is explicitly linearly equivalent to four copies of T. For a two-dimensional tensor factor it has 2^8 elements, and for scalar coefficients its coordinates agree with the normalized six-point coefficient heart Aug(F2^6)/<1>. The normalized dot product on that heart is proved bilinear, alternating, nondegenerate, and invariant under every word in the generated six-point action. After choosing a symplectic basis of the two-dimensional factor, the induced rank-eight tensor-product form is also proved alternating and nondegenerate, and every isotropic four-dimensional subspace is maximal isotropic. The explicit linear equivalence with two heart copies preserves this form and identifies the five projective-line packet members exactly with the diagonally stable maximal-isotropic subspaces of the rank-eight discriminant. In characteristic three, Lean constructs H3 as Aug(F3^6)/<1> and identifies it with four normalized augmentation coordinates. The quotient chart intertwines the induced translation and inversion actions with their displayed matrices and is an isometry for the minus-dot-product form descended through the constant line. The normalized symmetric form is nondegenerate and generator-invariant; the induced rank-eight tensor form is alternating, nondegenerate, and invariant under the diagonal generator actions. Exactly four four-dimensional subspaces are diagonally stable: the vertical half and three scalar graphs; all four are maximal isotropic. From the additional fibrewise kernel-coordinate input, Lean constructs an equivalence from every geometric kernel carrier to its displayed coordinate subspace and proves that every such transported kernel belongs to the five-member packet. Each labelled axis stabilizer in the concrete six-point action has ten elements and is the corresponding dihedral normalizer; its fixed subspace in the rational augmentation representation is exactly the line generated by the vector with coordinate 5 at that label and -1 elsewhere, and therefore has dimension one. The sum N of the ten stabilizer action operators has exactly that line as its range, satisfies N^2=10N, and after scaling by 1/10 is an idempotent projector onto the axis line. Every labelled axis stabilizer is self-normalizing. For any alternating-group action, if an object is fixed by the source stabilizer, then any two group elements carrying the source label to the same target carry that object to the same image. The six rational axis vectors sum to zero; their synthesis map has kernel exactly the constant line, is onto the augmentation representation, induces a linear equivalence from the six-coordinate quotient by the constant line, and intertwines the concrete alternating-group actions. Integrally, subtracting the sixth coordinate gives a linear equivalence from Z^6/Z1 to Z^5; the symmetric 6I6-J6 form descends through the constant line, and in this chart its Gram matrix is exactly 6I5-J5. Every permutation of the six labels induces a quotient map satisfying the identity and multiplication laws, and the descended form is invariant under all these maps.
claims.cautions: Coverage is fragmentary, not a conditional proof of the manuscript lemma: the theorem repackages opaque supplied geometric propositions while independently proving the arithmetic Smith witness and the coefficient-module parts of both primary discriminant calculations. Lean does not identify the explicit three-primary heart and tensor form with the geometric discriminant D3 = H3 tensor E[3], construct E[3] or its Weil pairing, or prove that the actual geometric three-primary kernel is one of the four formal maximal-isotropic halves. The coefficient-descent theorem proves only the rational representation-theoretic quotient and equivariance; it does not construct the six primitive elliptic-scheme inclusions, prove that their geometric sum is zero, or descend an actual homomorphism of abelian schemes. The integral quotient theorem constructs only the coefficient lattice and descended bilinear form; it does not identify them with an elliptic-power abelian scheme or geometric polarization. claims.hypotheses: The projective classification uses only finiteness and the field axioms. The concrete F4 trace-determinant, maximal-isotropic, and group-order calculations have no added mathematical hypothesis. Matching the human proof, the public trace-rigidity implication takes a supplied unit d in F4 and assumes that multiplication by d preserves the trace against every test element. The more general polarization theorem assumes exactly that a supplied slope is self-adjoint for a supplied pairing; finite-dimensionality is used for its half-dimension statement. One marked-F4 specialization takes a continuous classifier into the discrete affine chart Option F4; a stronger specialization takes a continuous classifier directly into Projectivization F4 (F4 x F4). These assume that one chosen fibre is one of the two scalar graphs defined by the transported marked root and its root+1 conjugate. The strongest persistence terminal replaces that marked-pair premise by the weaker premise that the chosen projective point is not fixed by coefficientwise Frobenius. The concrete stable-half terminal universally quantifies a subspace of two heart copies and characterizes the exact condition that it have F2-dimension four and be stable under the diagonal translation and inversion actions. The stronger polarization terminal requires no additional premise: it characterizes packet membership by diagonal stability and maximal isotropy. The explicit projective-line equivalence and its five marked chart values require no additional hypothesis.
claims.conclusion: Every projective-line point is uniquely vertical or a scalar graph; P1(F4) has five members and P1(F3) has four. The printed trace-determinant coefficient form and induced two-copy form are nondegenerate, every F4 scalar is self-adjoint, and every scalar graph equals its orthogonal complement, hence is maximal isotropic. Squaring on F4 is identified with the canonical Frobenius field automorphism; it fixes exactly 0 and 1, is involutive, and exchanges every other scalar with a distinct conjugate. On the affine projective chart it acts coefficientwise, fixes exactly the vertical point and graphs of 0 and 1, and its nonfixed locus is exactly the transported marked quadratic root together with root+1. Transporting that action through the proved affine-chart equivalence gives an involution directly on Projectivization F4 (F4 x F4), whose nonfixed locus is exactly the two scalar graph points of the marked root and root+1. The full five-letter symmetric group has order 120; its alternating subgroup has index two and full normalizer. Transported to this labelling, projective Frobenius is a transposition in the nontrivial coset, hence odd; its conjugation preserves both the alternating subgroup and the concrete PSL2(F4) projective image. A determinant unit whose multiplication preserves the trace against every test element is one. The concrete groups SL2(F4) and the alternating group on five letters both have order 60, the center of SL2(F4) is trivial, its faithful five-point projective image consists exactly of the even permutations, and the resulting construction gives an explicit abstract isomorphism SL2(F4) ≃ A5. Every continuous finite-discrete-packet classifying map on a connected base is constant, so membership in any distinguished subset at one fibre persists at every fibre. In particular, this is proved both for a continuous affine-chart F4 classifier and directly for a continuous classifier into the actual projective line when one chosen fibre lies in the marked two-point scalar-graph pair. More strongly, nonfixity under projective Frobenius at one fibre alone identifies that fibre with the marked pair and propagates the exact classification throughout the connected base. For the explicit six-point characteristic-two heart model, normalized representatives recover all four quotient coordinates, the coordinate kernel on the augmentation hyperplane is exactly the constant line, and translation and inversion induce the displayed matrices. The six labels are explicitly equivalent to the actual P1(F5); under this equivalence the two permutations are the projectivizations of (x,y) maps to (x,x+y) and (x,y) maps to (y,-x). These permutations preserve an explicit five-factor one-factorization; the induced factor words exhaust the alternating group on five letters and have exactly the same word kernel as the six-point words, so the generated six-point action is faithfully identified with a concrete A5. Lean constructs all six Sylow-five subgroups in this concrete A5 and proves that conjugation by the two generators acts on them by exactly the original six-point translation and inversion. The explicit P1(F5) labelling is therefore equivalent to the six-member Sylow-five packet. The faithful natural PSL2(F5) action has order 60; the two displayed permutations arise from explicit determinant-one matrices, and Lean constructs an isomorphism PSL2(F5) ≃ A5 that intertwines the full natural projective action with conjugation on the six Sylow-five subgroups. Both of these six-point actions are two-transitive. Every natural PSL2(F5) point stabilizer is proved to be the corresponding ten-element dihedral normalizer and is explicitly equivalent to D5. The six-label equivalence with the Sylow packet intertwines both generators with conjugation, and each point stabilizer is the corresponding normalizer. Each Sylow normalizer has ten elements and is explicitly equivalent to the dihedral group D5. Every subspace stable under both induced heart matrices is zero or the whole heart. A matrix commutes with every word matrix in the full generated heart action exactly when it is one of {0,1,W,W+1}, where W^2+W+1=0. A subspace of two heart copies is four-dimensional and stable under the diagonal generated action exactly when it is the vertical half or the graph of one of the four displayed commutant endomorphisms 0, 1, W, and W+1; the displayed packet has exactly five distinct members. An explicit equivalence with the actual P1(F4) sends the vertical chart point to the vertical half and the affine labels 0, 1, the transported marked root, and root+1 to the corresponding graphs of 0, 1, W, and W+1. The explicit alternating polarization form on the two heart copies is nondegenerate, and these five packet members are exactly the diagonally stable maximal-isotropic subspaces. The chosen linear equivalence from the standard rank-eight tensor discriminant coordinates to two heart copies preserves the bilinear form and transports this exact stable maximal-isotropic packet classification.
claims.cautions: Lean does not identify the six explicit Sylow-five subgroups and their dihedral normalizers with the manuscript's six geometrically named D5 normalizers. It therefore does not identify the proved concrete A5 permutation action, the resulting four-dimensional module, or its quadratic commutant with the manuscript's geometric A5 action, coefficient heart, and F4 commutant. It also does not prove that all geometrically A5-stable simple halves arise from the projective points, identify the geometric permutation stabilizer with the formalized SL2(F4), identify the manuscript's named A5 action with either formalized alternating-group model, prove that named subgroup lies in the stabilizer, classify the geometric S6 and A5 stabilizers, identify the manuscript's geometric odd normalizer element with the formalized Frobenius permutation, or construct the geometric local system, finite principal-kernel packet, or continuous classifying map needed to apply the connected-family persistence theorem. Thus the abstract generated-group, Sylow-five packet, dihedral normalizers, and six-point action identifications, six-point quotient coordinates and quadratic matrix commutant, finite-field enumeration, concrete polarization and maximal-isotropic algebra, determinant trace-rigidity, abstract exceptional-group identification, abstract Frobenius normalizer calculation, and exact connectedness deduction are checked, but the remaining geometric identifications remain absent. The arithmetic that selects the exotic pair is now covered: Lean computes the order of the symmetric group on six letters as 720 and proves that no group of smaller order, and no group of order 9720, admits an injective homomorphism from it, so none of the classified faithful automorphism groups of a smooth cubic threefold contains a copy of it. The classification supplying those orders remains an explicit hypothesis, and Lean does not construct cubic threefolds, their automorphism groups, or the descent of a stable kernel to an automorphism of the intermediate Jacobian.

claims.objects: Lean represents the two-by-two graph-coordinate block matrices over an arbitrary possibly noncommutative ring; actual rectangular coefficient and slope-error matrices of arbitrary finite block ranks over a commutative ring; a dependent family of finite blocks; the literal flattened square matrix on the disjoint union of all block bases; separately indexed base and split coordinates joined by a supplied invertible basis over a coefficient-extension ring; entrywise uniformizer-power divisibility; and the arithmetic cross-depth obtained by intersecting three divisibility conditions with an extended slope-difference valuation.

The rectangular positive-positive depth theorem uses finite block index types, a Mathlib discrete valuation domain, a chosen irreducible uniformizer, scalar slope parts, and arbitrary integral error matrices. The unit-positive theorem needs only a commutative ring, finite block indices, arbitrary integral slope matrices, and the positive-depth entrywise coefficient condition. The scalar lift-independence theorem uses the same DVR data.
claims.conclusion: The dual-form adjoint convention is equivalent to the coefficient-form convention for an invertible block. The displayed graph-coordinate product has exactly the manuscript's three nonzero blocks, and entrywise membership is equivalent to membership of those blocks. The actual rectangular commutator is A_ij T_j^t - T_i A_ij: the right slope error is transposed. The positive-positive and unit-positive calculations are assembled over a dependent family of finite blocks. Flattening to the disjoint union of block bases gives a literal symmetric weighted matrix lattice whose membership is exactly block symmetry plus all three graph-descent conditions, including diagonal entries and distinct entries within one block. After entrywise scalar extension and a supplied invertible basis change from distinct base coordinates to the flattened split axis, the transported matrix belongs to the weighted lattice exactly when its restricted blocks are symmetric and satisfy those graph-descent conditions. Positive-depth blocks use scalar plus depth-divisible error; at depth zero the error is unrestricted, so no finite-etale or scalar splitting is imposed. With finite flattened axis, the DVR graph cross-depth formula yields rank-one generation.

Lean checks the passage from any supplied splitting-ring basis and graph-descent block data through the transported flattened coefficient lattice and rank-one generation, but not the geometric construction that supplies those data or interprets the conditions as descended divisors.

More generally, congruence by a supplied invertible splitting-ring basis change preserves scalar rank-one forms, admits explicit inverse recovery, and allows the base and split coordinate types to differ. claims.conclusion: Lean proves the first line has norm five, the four complement vectors are orthogonal to it, their Gram matrix is exactly (6/5)(5I-J), det(5I-J)=125 is prime to two and three, and the four non-unit Smith entries have exact depth one at both primes. It also verifies that the displayed F2 slope model has minimal polynomial exactly t^2+t+1, by proving annihilation and irreducibility over F2. Over any supplied characteristic-two commutative ring containing a root omega, Lean identifies the literal same-pattern matrix with the entrywise scalar extension of the F2 matrix, and an explicit invertible basis diagonalizes it as diag(omega,omega+1,omega,omega+1). Lean additionally constructs the concrete root-adjoining extension, proves it finite etale of degree two over F2, constructs a coefficient-algebra equivalence with the concrete F4 used for the gluing packet, proves that the transported marked root lies outside {0,1}, that its Frobenius conjugate is exactly root+1, and that the corresponding two distinct affine-chart points form a projective-Frobenius two-cycle in the five-point gluing packet. It verifies the marked root equation and the same explicit two-sided eigenbasis and diagonalization both in the root-adjoining field and directly over the concrete F4 packet field. The displayed F3 model is literally scalar and commutes with every coefficient matrix.
claims.cautions: The two residue-field matrices are explicit algebraic models only. The concrete finite-etale theorem constructs the quadratic splitting extension of F2 for the displayed companion-block model and transports its marked root to one member of the two-element Frobenius orbit outside {0,1} in F4; the two exotic scalars are not otherwise individually named. It does not construct or identify the manuscript's marked geometric splitting extension. Lean does not prove that the actual six-axis geometric principal kernel or quotient graph has either model as its slope, does not identify the actual three-primary slope with a one-point finite-etale block, and does not prove persistence through the connected smooth component. Thus the geometric assertions about the actual kernels and slopes remain unformalized. The two finite F2 checks use ordinary kernel reduction via decide, with no native-code decision procedure, external certificate, or oracle; all remaining model claims are symbolic kernel-checked proofs. The passage from determinant prime-to-p to the formal Z_p notion of a unimodular lattice is represented arithmetically rather than through a dedicated p-adic lattice structure.

claims.objects: Lean represents a weighted matrix-of-ideals lattice, its internal rank-one span, a square-zero additive realization in a commutative ring, an abstract integral product subgroup, and explicit natural-number denominator witnesses for the resulting squarefree product representative.
claims.hypotheses: The lattice is exactly rank-one generated; every internal rank-one realization squares to zero; and for every prime p and every relevant finite internal presentation, some multiplier not divisible by p carries its squarefree degree-k product into the integral product subgroup. This is the elementwise denominator condition needed by the manuscript's local-to-global step; finite generation is unnecessary once these witnesses are supplied.
claims.conclusion: A finite internal rank-one presentation exists whose degree-k squarefree product belongs to the integral product subgroup globally and whose factorial multiple equals the kth power of the realized lattice element.
claims.cautions: The six-axis graph divisor lattice, its realization in cohomology, the local charts at two and three, the comparison away from six, production of the denominator witnesses from localization, and identification of divided powers with ordinary divisor products are not formalized here. In particular Lean does not yet prove membership of Theta^4/4! or any geometric divided-power claim, and the special-fibre Neron-Severi caution remains geometric.

claims.objects: A parameter type, a typed family of cubic-threefold objects, a separate type of intermediate-Jacobian objects, the intermediate-Jacobian assignment, predicates for smooth complex cubic status, algebraicity of the primitive minimal class, and universal CH0-triviality.
claims.hypotheses: Every indexed fibre is a smooth complex cubic threefold; the primitive minimal class of every fibre's intermediate Jacobian is algebraic; and for every smooth cubic under consideration Voisin's criterion identifies primitive-minimal-class algebraicity with universal CH0-triviality.
claims.conclusion: Every indexed fibre is universally CH0-trivial.
claims.cautions: Lean proves only the universally quantified logical deduction. The cubic pencil, smooth fibres, intermediate Jacobians, primitive minimal classes, their algebraicity from the six-axis divided-power theorem, Chow groups, universal base change in the CH0 predicate, and Voisin's geometric equivalence are represented by supplied types, functions, predicates, and premises rather than constructed. The argument is fibrewise and asserts neither a horizontal cycle nor a relative decomposition of the diagonal.

claims.objects: The coarse-moduli image of the nonstandard invariant cubic pencil of the alternating group on five letters, and cubic forms that split as sums of forms in pairwise disjoint nonempty groups of at most three variables.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness of the pencil members, and the separated-variable criterion for universal CH0-triviality of Colliot-Thelene.
claims.conclusion: Only finitely many moduli points of the pencil are represented by cubics projectively equivalent to a separated-variable form, so all but finitely many are universally CH0-trivial for a reason the separated-variable criterion does not supply.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. The projective-equivalence and dimension arguments over the coarse moduli image are outside the companion's scope.

claims.objects: The maximal A-model F-bundle of the ordinary Hodge-atom package, its intrinsic Euler field, the residual endomorphism of the connection in the loop coordinate, and the reduced spectral cover.
claims.hypotheses: The A-model connection conventions of the ordinary Hodge-atom package of Katzarkov, Kontsevich, Pantev, and Yu.
claims.conclusion: The residual endomorphism equals Euler multiplication with reversed sign, so the two operators share generalized eigenspaces and eigenvalue counts, and their reduced spectral covers correspond under negation.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. The companion contains no F-bundle, F-manifold, or spectral cover.

claims.objects: The Hodge-fixed locus of the maximal A-model F-bundle of a smooth projective variety, its tangent space, and the restriction of quantum multiplication to it.
claims.hypotheses: The rational classes of Hodge type (i,i) span the relevant subspace after extension to the Novikov coefficient field.
claims.conclusion: The Hodge-fixed locus is an F-submanifold whose multiplication and intrinsic Euler endomorphism are the restrictions of the ambient ones; for a smooth cubic threefold the Lefschetz theorem identifies it explicitly.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: The doubled Euler multiplication matrix and the grading matrix of the small even quantum connection of a smooth cubic threefold in the ordered classical basis, written over a characteristic-zero field in a nonzero square root r of three times the line-class Novikov variable; the constant separating change of basis; two explicit block-off-diagonal gauge coefficients; and the rank-two zero block with its canonical elementary modification.
claims.hypotheses: The field has characteristic zero and r is nonzero. No property of the two displayed connection matrices is assumed; they are the matrices exhibited in the source.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves that the separating change of basis has determinant -486 r^5, conjugates the Euler matrix to the diagonal pair 6r, -6r together with a single rank-two Jordan block at zero, and conjugates the grading matrix to the displayed separated form; that the two supplied gauge coefficients make the first and second coefficients of the transformed system block diagonal, with rank-two blocks diag(-19/18, 19/18) and the displayed second block; and that the residue of the canonical elementary modification is the displayed matrix, of trace -1 and determinant 5/36, whose characteristic polynomial is the rank-two indicial polynomial.
claims.cautions: This is a strictly weaker fragment of the manuscript statement. Lean verifies the supplied gauge coefficients rather than proving existence and uniqueness of the normalized gauge by the Sylvester recursion, and it stops at the second order, which is the order the residue needs. It does not construct the quantum connection and does not prove that the displayed matrices are the small even connection of a cubic threefold; that identification is the imported datum.

claims.objects: The residue discriminant of a rank-two spectral factor as a function on the base, and the vector fields of the Euler stratification acting on it.
claims.hypotheses: Regularity of Euler multiplication at the chosen base point.
claims.conclusion: The four displayed derivations of the discriminant hold on the germ, so the logarithmic differential of the discriminant is a regular one-form and the discriminant either is nowhere zero or vanishes identically on the germ.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: Eigenvalues of Euler multiplication on full cohomology and on even cohomology at an even point of the Hodge base.
claims.hypotheses: The base point lies in the even part of the Hodge base.
claims.conclusion: The two eigenvalue sets coincide.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: The small hyperplane point of the Hodge base of a smooth cubic threefold, the unramified reduced spectral cover above it, the parity ranks of its generalized eigenbundles, and the resulting ordinary Hodge atom.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness of the cubic threefold and the block reduction of small even Euler multiplication.
claims.conclusion: The small hyperplane point lies in the maximal-eigenvalue locus; the cover has two rank-one branches and one branch of parity ranks two and ten, and that rank-twelve branch is a connected component and hence defines a Hodge atom.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. The companion has no notion of Hodge atom or spectral component.

claims.objects: The Poincare pairing and the non-archimedean quantum connection.
claims.hypotheses: None beyond the algebraic setting; no convergence is assumed.
claims.conclusion: The pairing is horizontal for the connection.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: The leading operators of two local spectral factors, each a scalar plus a nilpotent matrix over a field, the off-diagonal blocks of the coefficients of the pairing between them, and block matrices assembled from two diagonal blocks and vanishing off-diagonal blocks.
claims.hypotheses: The two leading eigenvalues are distinct and the remaining parts of both leading operators are nilpotent; the leading order of horizontality gives the Sylvester equation for an off-diagonal coefficient; and at each later order the right-hand side vanishes once all strictly earlier off-diagonal coefficients vanish.
claims.conclusion: The Sylvester equation has only the zero solution, so every off-diagonal coefficient vanishes by induction on the order, and a pairing with vanishing off-diagonal blocks is invertible exactly when both diagonal restrictions are.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the F-bundle, the spectral splitting, the connection, or the pairing, and does not derive the order-by-order equations from horizontality; the shape of those equations, including that later right-hand sides involve only earlier coefficients, is a hypothesis. The refinement to the even part of a factor, which uses that the Poincare pairing pairs only equal parities, is not formalized.

claims.objects: The square-zero part of the centered leading Euler operator of an even rank-two atomic factor, the first two coefficients of the horizontal Poincare pairing in a chosen frame, and the regular coefficient of the connection in the loop direction, all as two-by-two matrices over a field in which two is invertible.
claims.hypotheses: The leading operator part squares to zero and is nonzero; the leading pairing coefficient is invertible; the leading operator part is self-adjoint for it; and the constant coefficient of horizontality relates the regular coefficient, the two pairing coefficients, and the leading operator part.
claims.conclusion: The regular coefficient carries the nilpotent line into itself, in the equivalent matrix form that the leading operator part, the regular coefficient, and the leading operator part again have vanishing product, together with its vector form: every vector in the image of the leading operator part is carried into its kernel.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the A-model F-bundle, the spectral cover, the atomic factor, or the Poincare pairing, and does not prove horizontality or nondegeneracy on a separated spectral factor; those supply the hypotheses. The line is presented as the image of the leading operator part rather than as a subobject of a geometric bundle.

claims.objects: The residual pole of the base connection in the modified lattice, written as a multiple of the lower-left matrix unit in the adapted frame; the residue of the modified lattice; and an additive Leibniz map of the coefficient ring applied entrywise, modelling a base derivation.
claims.hypotheses: For the first terminal, the upper-right entry of the residue is invertible, which it is, being the unit coming from the square-zero leading operator, and the order minus-one coefficient of flatness in the modified lattice vanishes. For the second, the entrywise derivation carries the residue to its commutator with a supplied regular matrix.
claims.conclusion: The residual pole vanishes, so the base connection is regular after the modification; and the derivation annihilates the residue discriminant, so that invariant is constant along the base.
claims.cautions: Lean formalizes the two algebraic steps and the conclusion, not the surrounding geometry: it does not construct the modified lattice, derive the displayed flatness coefficients from a connection, prove that the commutator equation follows from flatness, or run the completed-local-ring argument that upgrades a vanishing derivative to local constancy on a chart. The commutant computation identifying the leading base coefficient as a multiple of the leading operator part is also not formalized.

claims.objects: The residue of the canonical modified lattice as a two-by-two matrix over a commutative ring, together with two ring elements presented as its eigenvalues through its trace and determinant.
claims.hypotheses: The trace of the residue is the sum of the two supplied elements and its determinant is their product, which is what splitting the characteristic polynomial supplies.
claims.conclusion: The residue discriminant is the squared separation of the two eigenvalues, and it is unchanged by adding a scalar multiple of the identity to the residue, so it is insensitive to a scalar normalization.
claims.cautions: Only the second assertion of the proposition is formalized. The identification of the eigenvalue classes modulo the integers with the formal exponent classes of the centered rank-two module rests on the formal classification of regular-singular differential modules, which Lean does not construct, and the meromorphic gauge implementing the modification is not represented.

claims.objects: Local F-bundle factors over the unramified locus belonging to one connected component of the reduced spectral cover.
claims.hypotheses: The component is connected and the locus is unramified.
claims.conclusion: The factors glue up to regular block-diagonal change of frame, so any regular-gauge-invariant meromorphic expression built from the factor is a well-defined meromorphic function on the component.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: The residue discriminant as a meromorphic function on a connected spectral component.
claims.hypotheses: The leading nilpotent part is generically nonzero on the component.
claims.conclusion: The residue discriminant extends meromorphically and is constant on the component, so it does not depend on the base point representing the local atom.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: An ordinary Hodge atom whose geometric atomic F-bundle has even rank two, and the residue discriminant attached to it.
claims.hypotheses: The centered leading operator of the atomic F-bundle is generically nonzero nilpotent.
claims.conclusion: The residue discriminant is a well-defined invariant of the ordinary Hodge atom.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. This is the invariant the one-stabilization theorem runs on, and no part of its construction is in the companion.

claims.objects: The cubic atom and smooth projective varieties of dimension at most one.
claims.hypotheses: The computed values of the residue discriminant for the cubic atom and for curve atoms.
claims.conclusion: The cubic atom is represented by no smooth projective variety of dimension at most one.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: The cubic atom and smooth projective surfaces, together with the classification of minimal surfaces and parity ranks.
claims.hypotheses: The preceding curve exclusion and additivity of atoms for disjoint unions.
claims.conclusion: The cubic atom is represented by no smooth projective surface, hence by no smooth projective variety of dimension at most two.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. The surface classification input is imported classical geometry.

claims.objects: Lean represents a supplied finite complex matrix declared to be the framed formal-monodromy operator; it does not construct the small even quantum connection or its Levelt--Turrittin monodromy.
claims.hypotheses: The matrix is already the operator for one turn of the original unramified z-disc, on a labelled finite-dimensional complex vector space.
claims.conclusion: The invariant is the sum of the characteristic-polynomial root multiplicities at exp(pi*i/3) and exp(-pi*i/3).
claims.cautions: The type records the framed operator only after construction; it neither permits nor models adjoining roots of z, and it does not prove independence of the algebraic closure.

claims.objects: Bulk shifts of the even quantum connection by a multiple of the identity and by a divisor class, and the framed formal-monodromy eigenvalues on the original loop disc.
claims.hypotheses: The coefficient field contains the Novikov coefficients of the connection, and the divisor shift defines a multiplicative character on the numerical Novikov image.
claims.conclusion: The identity shift changes the connection only by a scalar irregular twist and leaves the framed eigenvalues unchanged; the divisor shift acts by a coefficient substitution fixing the complex numbers, so it preserves the algebraic multiplicity of every root of unity.
claims.cautions: Not formalized as stated. The manuscript no longer routes this through the pro-Laurent gauge machinery that the companion formalizes.

claims.objects: Three nested algebraic branches are represented. The general coefficient-pushforward branch has effective homological and numerical additive monoids, a possibly nonsurjective quotient, compatible natural-valued degree functions, finite bounded homological pieces, and ordinary or completed coefficient families. The completed-convolution branch has one additive monoid with an additive natural grading, finite bounded pieces, and compatible systems of finite additive-monoid-algebra truncations. The completed numerical-ring branch adds finite bounded numerical pieces, a surjective degree-compatible quotient, finite coefficient packets, and additive scalar-weight homomorphisms for logarithmic Novikov operators.
claims.hypotheses: In the general branch, ordinary pushforward uses additive-commutative-monoid coefficients, while completed additive pushforward uses additive-commutative-group coefficients; its elementary cutoff-agreement theorem assumes equality of the two source families through the chosen cutoff. The convolution, `AgreeThrough`, and cutoff-continuity terminals use commutative-ring coefficients. The finite-packet terminal uses additive-commutative-monoid coefficients and explicitly assumes that its coefficient function is constant on numerical fibers. The compatible-family pushforward terminal assumes a surjective quotient with exact degree compatibility, finite bounded gradings on both sides, and commutative-ring coefficients. The standalone Leibniz terminal assumes one finite-degree additive monoid, commutative-ring coefficients, and an additive scalar weight. Its numerical pushforward-commutation terminal additionally supplies an additive numerical weight whose homological weight is the quotient pullback.
claims.conclusion: Ordered additive decompositions are finite and exact; convolution gives completed coefficient families a commutative-ring structure and agrees through every cutoff with ordinary additive-monoid-algebra multiplication. Completed coefficient families are equivalent, by mutually inverse reconstruction maps, to compatible systems of finite degree truncations. Under this equivalence, numerical pushforward is levelwise the ordinary additive-monoid-algebra map induced by the quotient, and the completed/truncation square commutes exactly. Addition, convolution, and numerical pushforward preserve coefficient agreement through the same cutoff, so numerical pushforward satisfies the explicit cutoff-continuity predicate with identity modulus. Finite-fiber numerical summation preserves finite-below support and cutoff agreement, commutes exactly with finite truncation, preserves convolution and the unit, and defines a unital ring homomorphism. Finite coefficient packets constant on numerical fibers descend termwise and fiber sums are cardinality multiples of the descended coefficient. The coefficientwise operator associated to an additive scalar weight is an additive homomorphism and satisfies the Leibniz rule for completed convolution; completed pushforward commutes with this operator when the weight factors through the quotient.
claims.cautions: The general coefficient-pushforward quotient need not be surjective. The completed numerical pushforward is proved to be a ring homomorphism when its monoid quotient is surjective; Lean does not assert that this ring homomorphism is itself surjective. The formal completed rings are coefficient families with a finite-below support condition. Their explicit compatible-truncation object and type equivalence are coefficientwise. Cutoff continuity is a quantified coefficient-agreement predicate, not Mathlib topological continuity; no topology, uniform space, categorical limit cone, or universal property in a category of topological rings is represented. The finite-type Chow-variety proof of bounded finiteness is supplied as a hypothesis rather than formalized. Lean assumes rather than proves numerical invariance of the finite coefficient packet, and it does not identify that packet with Gromov--Witten invariants. The weighted operator is packaged additively but is not bundled as a scalar-linear derivation over a separately modeled coefficient subring. Quantum products and connections, curve pushforward and normal-bundle pairings, geometric construction of the additive curve-pairing weights, and base change of the quantum comparison isomorphisms are not represented.

claims.objects: The even quantum connection pulled back to a formal smooth bulk germ, an isolated rank-two Euler cluster, and the residue of its canonical elementary modification.
claims.hypotheses: The coefficient field is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, the cluster's nilpotent part is a single nonzero Jordan block at the closed point, and every other Euler eigenvalue differs from it by a unit.
claims.conclusion: The cluster stays a single nonzero Jordan block on the germ, the residue has constant characteristic polynomial there, and the primitive-sixth multiplicities contributed by the block are constant on the germ.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. The companion's formal-germ material treats gauge and base-change invariance rather than this rigidity statement.

claims.objects: A supplied type of geometric objects with relations for a rank-r projective bundle and a codimension-c smooth-center blowup; dependent numerical Novikov specializations; and intrinsic and specialized finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrices.
claims.hypotheses: For r at least two, the projective-bundle relation is supplied together with equality of its intrinsic characteristic polynomial to the r-th power of the base polynomial. For c at least two, the blowup relation is supplied together with c-1 center specializations and equality of the total characteristic polynomial to the ambient polynomial times the finite product of the specialized center polynomials.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves the exact framed operation formulas: projective-bundle primitive-sixth multiplicity is r times the base multiplicity, and blowup multiplicity is the ambient multiplicity plus the sum of the c-1 specialized center multiplicities.
claims.cautions: The result is conditional on the geometric and characteristic-polynomial comparison inputs. Lean does not construct varieties, vector bundles, projective bundles, smooth centers, blowups, endpoint or specialized-center quantum connections, Iritani comparison coordinates, parity restrictions, numerical Novikov specializations, or the characteristic-polynomial block identities. No loop-coordinate root is represented.

claims.objects: Lean represents an effective additive monoid, a complete separated topological commutative domain, a multiplicative monomial-image function, a natural-valued length, and a natural-valued valuation.
claims.hypotheses: The monomial image preserves zero and addition, every monomial image is nonzero, valuation equals length on monomials, length is positive off zero and proper on bounded sets, and valuation is additive on products of nonzero target elements.
claims.conclusion: A typed certificate for the algebraic and topological core of strict Novikov admissibility.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the numerical Novikov completion or the associated graded ring; global valuation multiplicativity records the no-product-cancellation input but is not yet proved equivalent to the manuscript's domain associated-graded condition.

claims.objects: The specialized framed sixth-root count of a smooth projective target under a strictly Novikov-admissible specialization, for nef-canonical targets, the projective line and plane, and geometrically ruled surfaces over positive-genus curves.
claims.hypotheses: Strict Novikov admissibility of the specialization; for the ruled-surface case only, the reconstruction-tail hypothesis of this section.
claims.conclusion: The count vanishes unconditionally in the nef-canonical case and for the projective line and plane, and vanishes for ruled surfaces over positive-genus curves under the reconstruction-tail hypothesis.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. The Lean low-dimensional vanishing material is registered under the conditional low-dimensional vanishing claim, which is the combined statement rather than these direct cases.

claims.objects: A supplied type of geometric objects with dependent strictly Novikov-admissible specializations and intrinsic, divisor-tagged, and specialized finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrices, all over C; separately, the algebraic strict-Novikov certificate, an individual-class tag map, a finite injective vector family over an infinite characteristic-zero field, a completed coefficient family with finite support below every length cutoff, an injective integral divisor-pairing vector, an additive tagged-image map into an additive target, monomial initial coefficients, and direction-dependent initial-form detectors valued in one-variable formal power series.
claims.hypotheses: For every supplied strictly Novikov-admissible specialization, the final common-field polynomial equality resulting from the unformalized coefficient extension and algebraic-closure identifications is supplied, as is the final polynomial equality resulting from the unformalized divisor-equation formal bulk gauge. The individual-class theorem assumes that the tag separates numerical classes. The abstract finite-family theorem assumes an injective vector family over an infinite characteristic-zero field. For the completed tagging injection, the integral pairing vector is injective over an arbitrary characteristic-zero coefficient field; every monomial initial coefficient is nonzero; every direction detector sends zero to zero; and, for every nonzero completed series and integral direction, the detected initial form of its tagged image is supplied to equal the finite exponential-character combination on the formalized lowest support.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves equality of intrinsic and specialized primitive-sixth multiplicities and transfers intrinsic vanishing through every strictly Novikov-admissible specialization. It proves injectivity of the paired monomial/class tag on individual numerical classes. For every finite injective vector family, it chooses an abstract K-linear separator and proves finite exponential-character independence; for integral pairing families it constructs an integral direction. At coefficient level, every nonzero completed series has a nonempty finite lowest support and exponential-character noncancellation over every characteristic-zero field. From the supplied initial-form compatibility and nonzero monomial initial coefficients, Lean proves the tagged image of every nonzero series is nonzero, reflects zero, and is fully injective by applying noncancellation to differences.
claims.cautions: The vanishing result remains conditional on two final polynomial equalities over C. No source coefficient fields, common comparison field, embeddings, Polynomial.map scalar extension, or typed bulk-gauge witness occur in that theorem. The associated-graded tagging interface neither represents nor constructs the filtered target ring, associated graded ring, valuation, or geometric Novikov specialization. It supplies only proxy detector functions, their zero values, nonzero monomial initial coefficients, and the compatibility equality, and does not prove that they arise from the manuscript's filtered hypotheses. Lean proves the exact noncancellation and injectivity deduction from these proxy inputs. The individual-class injection alone does not imply completed-series injection; the latter uses the compatibility package. Construction of the integral divisors whose pairing vectors separate numerical curve classes, common algebraic closures, scalar extension of quantum connections, the divisor-equation bulk pullback, and compatible integral-loop-power finite-quotient gauges also remain unformalized.

claims.objects: A supplied type of geometric objects with a predicate for points, smooth projective curves, and smooth projective surfaces; a nef-seed predicate; a named point and projective-bundle and point-blowup relations; dependent strictly Novikov-admissible specializations; and intrinsic and specialized finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrices.
claims.hypotheses: Every selected object has a supplied inductive classification witness built from a nef seed, the point, a positive-rank projective bundle, or a point blowup. Nef-seed characteristic roots are supplied to have square one; the point multiplicity is zero; the projective-bundle formula multiplies the base multiplicity by the rank; point blowup preserves multiplicity; and divisor tagging transfers intrinsic vanishing to each strictly Novikov-admissible specialization.
claims.conclusion: For every supplied point, smooth projective curve, or smooth projective surface and every strictly Novikov-admissible specialization, the specialized framed monodromy has primitive-sixth multiplicity zero. Lean proves the classification induction, including the exact root-square-one spectral endpoint, and the final specialization transfer. A separate corollary proves that matrix involutivity is a stronger sufficient condition for the spectral restriction.
claims.cautions: The result is conditional on every geometric and comparison input used by the human proof. Lean does not construct the varieties, quantum connections, framed monodromy, numerical Novikov rings, grading operator or parity correction; prove regular singularity and nilpotence of the residue; derive the plus-or-minus-one spectrum from nefness; prove the low-dimensional minimal-model classification; construct the projective bundles or blowups; establish their monodromy formulas; or prove divisor tagging and specialization comparison. The human proof restricts eigenvalues to {1,-1}; it does not assert involutivity of the full monodromy matrix, which is strictly stronger in the presence of possible Jordan parts and appears only in the separately marked sufficient corollary.

claims.objects: An arbitrary carrier type with natural-valued multiplicity and dimension, explicit smooth-projective-complex and smooth-center predicates, typed blowup steps in either orientation, and specialized center contributions.
claims.hypotheses: Smooth endpoints; source dimension at most four; every blowup step has codimension at least two, the center-plus-codimension dimension identity, preserved ambient dimension, and the displayed additive operation formula; every specialized contribution of a smooth center of dimension at most two vanishes; and a composable typed weak-factorization chain is supplied.
claims.conclusion: Equality of multiplicities at the endpoints, obtained by proving each typed blowup or blowdown link preserves multiplicity and telescoping the chain.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct varieties, quantum connections, comparison specializations, operation formulas, low-dimensional vanishing, or the AKMW factorization chain; those remain typed data.  The older abstract preserving-chain terminal is retained and is strictly weaker than the typed telescope.

claims.objects: A rank-one generalized eigenspace of Euler multiplication for the even quantum connection at an even bulk point, and its contribution to framed regular monodromy.
claims.hypotheses: The target is smooth projective and the coefficient field is algebraically closed.
claims.conclusion: Such a block contributes only the eigenvalue one, so at the small point it contributes nothing to the framed sixth-root count.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.

claims.objects: The framed sixth-root count of a product of a smooth projective variety with a projective space.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness and projectivity of the factor; the product formula for Gromov-Witten theory and the multiplicity-one Euler block lemma.
claims.conclusion: The count of the product is the count of the factor multiplied by one more than the dimension of the projective space, unconditionally.
claims.cautions: Not formalized as stated. The formula enters the two product-formula corollaries as an explicit typed premise, and the companion's projective-bundle formula is registered under the conditional framed operation claim and is proved under the reconstruction-tail hypothesis, whereas this product statement is unconditional.

claims.objects: A supplied type of varieties with a distinguished point, the projective spaces, the product of a variety with a projective space, and the framed sixth-root count of each of them.
claims.hypotheses: The product formula multiplies the count of a variety by one more than the dimension of the projective factor; a projective space is the product of the point with that projective space; and the framed monodromy of the point is involutive.
claims.conclusion: Lean deduces that the point has vanishing count and hence that every projective space has vanishing count, including three-space and four-space.
claims.cautions: The product formula is a typed premise: Lean does not construct varieties, products, quantum connections, or framed monodromy, and does not prove the Gromov-Witten product formula or the compatibility of the formal decomposition with tensor products used in the manuscript's proof of that formula. Involutivity of the framed monodromy of the point stands for the manuscript's rank-one trivial connection at a point.

claims.objects: A supplied type of cubic objects with a smooth-complex-cubic-threefold predicate and a finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrix; Cai's rank-two indicial polynomial and the displayed characteristic polynomial with one factor for each primitive sixth root and two unit factors.
claims.hypotheses: For every supplied smooth cubic threefold, the framed-monodromy characteristic polynomial is supplied to equal the displayed four-factor polynomial arising from Cai's integral-loop-power block description.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves the indicial roots -1/6 and -5/6 give the negative and positive primitive sixth roots, proves those roots are distinct and each has algebraic multiplicity one while the two unit factors contribute nothing, and concludes that every supplied smooth cubic threefold has primitive-sixth multiplicity exactly two. A second terminal reaches the same value from a weaker premise: it assumes only that framed monodromy exponentiates the exponents of the reduced system, with two unit factors from the rank-one blocks, and proves which exponents occur from the block reduction.
claims.cautions: The result is conditional on the characteristic-polynomial comparison. Lean does not construct a smooth cubic threefold, its numerical small even quantum connection, Cai's integral-loop-power block diagonalization, the rank-two zero-exponential block, the two remaining rank-one unit blocks, or the identification of their direct-sum characteristic polynomial with the supplied framed monodromy. Lean also does not prove that the cubic threefold's numerical curve lattice has rank one or that the manuscript's numerical-Novikov convention leaves Cai's calculation unchanged. The second terminal removes the characteristic-polynomial assumption in favour of the exponent-to-monodromy passage, which remains external; the exponents themselves are now derived from the displayed connection matrices.

claims.objects: The primitive-sixth multiplicity of a smooth cubic threefold throughout the formal even bulk germ at the small hyperplane point.
claims.hypotheses: Extension of the cubic Novikov coefficient field making the square root of three times the line variable a unit, together with formal-germ rigidity of the isolated rank-two packet.
claims.conclusion: The multiplicity equals two throughout that germ.
claims.cautions: Not formalized. The Lean cubic packet material proves the value at the small point from a supplied characteristic polynomial and does not propagate it over a formal germ.

claims.objects: A supplied type of varieties with a smooth-cubic-threefold predicate, framed monodromy, and the product of a variety with a projective space; the rank-two indicial polynomial of the reduced small even system.
claims.hypotheses: The product formula multiplies the count by one more than the dimension of the projective factor. The first terminal assumes the count of the base variety is two; the second assumes instead that framed monodromy exponentiates the exponents of the reduced system with two unit factors, and derives the value two from the block reduction.
claims.conclusion: The count of the product with a projective line is four; for the second terminal this holds for every supplied smooth cubic threefold.
claims.cautions: The product formula remains a typed premise, as does the passage from residue exponents to framed formal monodromy. Lean constructs neither the varieties and their products nor the quantum connections, and the companion's separate projective-bundle formula is proved only under the reconstruction-tail hypothesis registered with the conditional framed operation claim.

claims.objects: An abstract geometric signature naming smooth prime genus-eight Fano threefolds, their associated Pfaffian cubics, both rank-two projective-bundle total spaces, product with projective one-space, projective four-space, and rationality.
claims.hypotheses: The specified carrier satisfies the genus-eight predicate, its associated cubic satisfies the smooth-cubic predicate, both named total spaces obey the rank-two formulas and are birational, the cubic packet is two, and the named stabilization and rational comparison have the stated properties.
claims.conclusion: The specified Fano carrier has packet multiplicity two and its named product with projective one-space is irrational.
claims.cautions: The geometric signature and the Kuznetsov, quantum, weak-factorization, and rational-comparison facts remain typed premises rather than foundational constructions. Lean follows the framed route, which the manuscript states conditionally; the manuscript's unconditional half, obtained by comparing the two projective bundles birationally and applying the atomic one-step theorem, has no Lean terminal.
